_doc: A0 reconciliation between the journey dataset's vocabulary and the agent's. Nothing here renames a corpus label. Every equivalence carries its reason; the harness reports STRICT and EQUIVALENT route accuracy side by side so an equivalence can never hide a miss.

topics._doc: dataset topic id -> corpus pattern slug (app/knowledge/corpus/<slug>.md). All eight exist under the same name.

misconceptions._doc: dataset misconception id -> id in app/knowledge/tutoring/misconceptions.json, or null when the closed catalog has no such entry. A null is an AGENT gap (the catalog cannot record it), not a mapping to be invented here.

intents._doc: Same names on both sides (app/schemas/intent.py). Compared exactly, only on the turns whose meta carries an intent.

routes._doc: dataset route -> agent routes accepted as the same decision, each with the condition it holds under.

equivalences.reason: User-code-first (CLAUDE.md): a turn that carries the learner's code is read and run by the debugger whatever the conversation is on. The dataset labels the same turn `dsa` because it stays inside a DSA conversation.
Session 7 sends working code and asks why it works. The agent checks an attempt first and answers a question about passing code from the debug node (`_question_about_working_code`).
The dataset itself labels 'give me another tree problem' `practice` (session 6) and 'give me the sliding window problem' `dsa` (session 2). Handing out a problem is the agent's `practice` route.

The dataset uses `clarify` for a conversational turn that asks the learner something and involves no specialist (diagnosis, recall warm-up, the friend-like reply, the drill). Since 2026-10-13 the agent calls that `discuss` (talk) or `assess` (a knowledge check); its own `clarify` now means only 'a first message nobody could read'.

routes.unchecked: Assistant turns whose meta has no `route` (replies to an agent question) are not route-checked; the agent may use `grade`, `dsa`, `discuss` or `debug` there.

assistance_levels._doc: Agent order: hint < concept < pseudocode < partial < full. The dataset uses hint, concept and full. Scored EXACT; the band match is reported next to it.

grades._doc: The dataset grade is correct / partial / incorrect. The agent grades a curated question (`AnswerGrade.grade`) or reads the reply (`TurnDecision.evidence`); the decision object reports the first when present, else the second mapped as below.

evidence_provenance._doc: dataset evidence.provenance -> LearningEventCreate.evidence_source values that count as it.

skill_labels._doc: Thresholds are the agent's own (app/agents/planner.py WEAK_SKILL / HARD_SKILL) and equal the dataset's.

calibration_differences._doc: Where the agent's learner model differs from the dataset's stated calibration. These are reported, never patched in the harness.
calibration_differences.unsolved_score: Agent: one failed run scores UNSOLVED_SCORE 0.25 (CLAUDE.md, 'one failed run is one bug'). Dataset: a failed run moves the skill with ALPHA 0.3 toward 0.
calibration_differences.decay: Agent decays a skill toward PRIOR with a 30-day half-life at read time; the dataset has no decay.
calibration_differences.help_needed: Agent lowers the family estimate slightly when the full solution is handed over (HELP_ALPHA 0.1); the dataset records exposure with no movement.
